`name="email"` and `name = "email"` mean the same thing. Using one style everywhere keeps props easy to scan. By default the rule allows no space on either side of the `=`.

`--fix` adds or removes the spaces.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```jsx
const field = <input name = "email" />;
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
const field = <input name="email" required />;
```

## Options

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `"never"` (default) | Allow no space before or after the `=`. |
| `"always"` | Require a space before and after the `=`. |

{/* bad {"options": ["always"]} */}
```jsx
const field = <input name="email" />;
```

{/* good {"options": ["always"]} */}
```jsx
const field = <input name = "email" />;
```

## When not to use it

A formatter such as `bun format` or Prettier already fixes this spacing.
